entities.summary:
The asteroid belt is a circumstellar disk in an orbit around the sun between those of Mars and Jupiter, spanning approximately 200 million kilometers in width. Formed around 4.6 billion years ago during the late heavy bombardment period, it is a remnant of the solar system's early formation and contains millions of small rocky bodies, including dwarf planet Ceres and the asteroid Vesta. The asteroid belt's significance lies in its role as a source of meteorites that have impacted Earth, providing insights into the solar system's early history and the composition of the early solar planets. The belt's location also makes it a crucial region for understanding the formation and evolution of the inner solar system. 

The asteroid belt has been the subject of scientific study and exploration since the 17th century, with the first recorded observation of the belt being made by Giovanni Cassini in 1675. The discovery of asteroids within the belt in the 19th century led to a greater understanding of its structure and composition. The 20th century saw the development of space agencies and spacecraft capable of exploring the asteroid belt, including NASA's Dawn mission, which orbited the dwarf planet Ceres in 2015-2016.

The asteroid belt's legacy can be seen in the many meteorites that have fallen to Earth, providing valuable information about the early solar system's composition and evolution. The belt's influence on the formation and evolution of the inner solar system is also evident in the many asteroids that have been found to have originated from the belt. The study of the asteroid belt continues to be an active area of research, with ongoing and future missions aimed at exploring the region in greater detail.
